claim: Shared learned Q improves terminal discovery reliability per proposal-native tick over the random-valid and structured baselines, but it does not optimize route cost. Under the common 1427-tick whole-decision cutoff, learned reaches terminal in 5/8 decisions with best cost 147, structured reaches terminal in 3/7 decisions with best cost 130, and random-valid reaches terminal in 1/2 decisions with best cost 160. Learned generation two repeats the first 147-tick terminal instead of improving it, while structured search finds 130. P5 therefore remains unsatisfied.

bindings.terminal: authenticated F_SP103 to F_SP104 load-zone commit

workload.equal_budget_rule: Retain deterministic seed-order decisions only when the entire four-proposal decision fits within 1427 proposal-native ticks. Post-run macro validation is reported separately and excluded from this learning-policy cutoff.

framework_defects_closed_during_comparis: Random-valid now consumes the same live applicability mask as learned and structured policies.
A bounded observation-driven tactic may terminate unsuccessfully before the enclosing batch horizon without being mislabeled as an invalid learning observation.
Native suffix validation accepts early unsuccessful completion only for controller-program candidates; static and frozen-policy candidates retain exact horizon checks.
Rust controller re-inference now reproduces the native coordinate-sequence final-target terminal state.

interpretation.throughput: All treatments finish in roughly 49-51 wall seconds despite 2.8x variation in proposal-native ticks. Native simulation occupies 14-35 seconds, while preparation and evidence persistence consume substantial additional time. More raw mining would spend most learned budget repeating the 147-tick terminal and would not address the cost objective.
interpretation.learning: The critic is useful for finding a terminal cheaply and reliably, but terminal reward dominates cost sensitivity. Later shared generations collapse onto the first successful 147-tick tactic. Structured search reaches a 130-tick route within a comparable native budget, disproving a learned route-quality advantage.
interpretation.random_baseline: Random-valid has the broadest coverage and ultimately matches the 130-tick structured best, but it requires 3650 proposal-native ticks to do so. Its 6/8 unnormalized success rate is not evidence that it beats learned search.
interpretation.next_engineering_target: Make successful-terminal value explicitly cost-conditioned and reserve acquisition capacity for refinements below the best observed terminal cost. Then rerun fixed-generation treatments under an enforced proposal-native tick budget. In parallel, reduce persistence/preparation overhead; raw native simulator speed is not the sole end-to-end bottleneck.
